description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of performance percentages across different score intervals for a model evaluation, likely from the paper “Can 1B LLM Surpass 405B LLM? Rethinking Compute-Optimal Test-Time Scaling.” The horizontal axis represents score bins ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, while the vertical axis shows the percentage of instances falling within each bin, scaled from 0.0 to 0.8. Four light blue bars correspond to the bins [0.0, 0.2), [0.2, 0.4), [0.4, 0.6), and [0.6, 0.8), with labeled percentages of 11.2%, 3.4%, 3.4%, and 5.8% respectively. A significantly taller bar spans the [0.8, 1.0] bin, labeled 76.2%, indicating a strong concentration of high-performing results. A red dashed vertical line at approximately 0.82 marks the mean score, with the annotation “mean: 0.82” in red text positioned near the top of the chart. The chart visually emphasizes that the majority of evaluations achieve scores above 0.8, suggesting high overall performance, possibly for a smaller 1B parameter LLM under test-time scaling strategies. A small gray rectangle is present below the x-axis between 0.4 and 0.6, though its purpose is not labeled and may be a placeholder or artifact.
